args.text:
DETROIT, Dec. 13 (AP).—Henry Ford's first big crack at his already announced push to teach the American public the old-fashioned square dances'll be on Tuesday night at one of the biggest dance halls in Detroit. For the do, Mr. Ford is advertisin' for couples to dance the square dance and to make up the core of the party.

Asked tonight whether he really reckoned the old-fashioned steps'd come back, Mr. Ford sang out:

"Come back? They're here! We simply are falling back in line. What we are trying to do in getting out a book of dances is to standardize them. The first edition is being revised in the direction of simplicity."

Out of the twenty-one quadrilles, Mr. Ford explained, four'll be picked to make 'em easier to teach and get more people keen on 'em.

"Mellie" Dunham, the champion fiddler of Maine, who's been stayin' as Mr. Ford's guest for a week, playin' for an old-fashioned dance party and chippin' in several old-time tunes for the Ford "Americana" of such pieces now bein' got ready for publishin', was meant to turn out at the Tuesday night do. But the plans got changed and "Grandpa Mellie," with the missus, is on his way tonight to New York, where he might answer the call of the footlights and sign up for a vaudeville contract.

"Mellie" Dunham'll front up in New York this mornin'. It was reported last night that he'll be under the management of Tex Rickard, who's said to be plannin' a barn dance in his honour at the brand-spankin'-new Madison Square Garden. It was added that puttin' on this dance was hoped to help along Henry Ford's aim of makin' square dances popular again.
